# filters.ekf { #wdm.filters.ekf }

`filters.ekf`

Extended Kalman filter using JAX automatic differentiation.

Included for comparison rather than as the default. The extended filter
linearises the transition about the current mean,

$$
F_k = \left. \frac{\partial f}{\partial z} \right|_{z = \hat z_k},
$$

and propagates covariance through that linear map. Historically this meant
deriving and maintaining Jacobians by hand -- error-prone, and the single most
common source of silent bugs in filtering code. With ``jax.jacfwd`` the Jacobian
is exact to machine precision and free to obtain, which removes that objection
entirely and leaves only the approximation-quality one.

That remaining objection is real. Linearisation is first-order accurate; the
unscented transform is third-order for Gaussian inputs. Where the two disagree
on this model, the unscented answer is the one to believe. Running both is a
genuinely informative diagnostic: large divergence means the posterior is
spread over a region where the dynamics are meaningfully curved, which is itself
worth knowing.

## Functions

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [extended_filter](#wdm.filters.ekf.extended_filter) | Forward extended-filtering pass with a linear observation. |

### extended_filter { #wdm.filters.ekf.extended_filter }

```python
filters.ekf.extended_filter(
    transition,
    process_cov,
    h,
    obs_var,
    m0,
    p0,
    inputs,
    y,
    observed,
    *,
    gate_sigma=4.0,
    dof=None,
)
```

Forward extended-filtering pass with a linear observation.

Signature matches `wdm.filters.ukf.unscented_filter` so the two can be
swapped without touching call sites.
